subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'taught'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence structure indicates that the author is referring to lessons learned from past experiences.
 
• "Taught" is the past tense of "teach," which aligns with the retrospective nature of the statement.
 
• Using "taught" suggests that the lessons have already been learned, fitting the context of reflecting on past experiments.
 
• The phrase "past experiments" signals that the action (teaching) occurred in the past, hence the past tense "taught" is appropriate.
 
• "Taught them" implies that policymakers have learned something from previous reforms.
 
• The use of "taught" completes the logical flow of the sentence, emphasizing the importance of learning from history to avoid repeating mistakes.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Teaching" (Option 1): Incorrect because it is a gerund or present participle, which doesn't fit the past context.
 
• "Teaches" (Option 2): Incorrect because it is present tense and does not align with the past reference.
 
• "Will teach" (Option 3): Incorrect because it is future tense and does not match the reflection on past experiences.
